subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw keep `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` as a documented break-glass mode, harden it with additional browser CSRF defenses, or remove it with compatibility handling?
rationale: The exact reproduction is overbroad, but the remaining behavior is an intentional security downgrade in a shipped config surface, so automation should not decide whether to break or preserve that operator path.

options.title: Harden the fallback
options.body: Keep the documented flag but add focused defense-in-depth and tests for same-host/DNS-rebinding browser requests before accepting the risk.

options.title: Remove the fallback
options.body: Delete the flag and add upgrade/docs handling for operators who currently rely on Host-header origin policy.

options.title: Accept current dangerous mode
options.body: Document that the existing critical audit warning and startup log are sufficient, and close this as an accepted operator-controlled risk.

recommendation.title: Harden the fallback
recommendation.body: Keep the documented flag but add focused defense-in-depth and tests for same-host/DNS-rebinding browser requests before accepting the risk.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the closest merged gateway origin hardening path and is the strongest current-history route for the HTTP/trusted-proxy side of the boundary.
